title: Fin Box Skin Laminate — Scarf Repair After Lightning Attachment
abstract: Permanent scarf repair for delamination and surface burning in the fin box skin laminate after a lightning attachment, including restoration of the conductive mesh continuity across the repair.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the laminate strength and the lightning current path of the fin box skin after a lightning attachment has caused local delamination, resin loss or surface burning.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the delamination by ultrasonic inspection over a radius of at least 250 mm from the attachment point, and mark the boundary on the surface. Measure the depth of resin loss and the number of plies affected by tap test and by ultrasonic through-transmission where access allows. Damage that stays inside the allowable limits below may be sealed and left under repeat inspection. Damage that reaches a spar or rib foot, that affects more than four plies, or that lies within 150 mm of an existing repair, is outside the scope of this repair. Measure and record the bonding resistance at the two nearest rib feet before you start, because the repair must restore it.
sections.repair_procedure: Mark the scarf boundary at the ratio given on the repair drawing and remove the damaged plies by controlled sanding, working ply by ply and confirming each ply removal by the colour change of the fabric. Do not use a router. Clean the scarf with the approved solvent and dry it under heat to the schedule on the drawing. Lay up the replacement plies in the orientation sequence of the drawing, adding one extra ply over the scarf edge on the outer surface. Fit the composite repair strap D5170129418478 across the repair where the damage boundary crosses a stringer land. Restore the conductive mesh across the repair using the mesh patch supplied with the repair kit, overlapping the existing mesh by the dimension on the drawing, and bond the fitting VAL343190-19 at the mesh termination. Cure under vacuum with the heat blanket to the schedule on the drawing and record the thermocouple trace. Sand the cured surface to the profile, restore the surface protection and the external paint scheme. Measure the bonding resistance at the two nearest rib feet and confirm that it is at or below the value recorded before the repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 15 000 flight hours from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat tap test and ultrasonic inspection of the repair boundary every 5 000 flight hours, and a bonding resistance measurement at the two nearest rib feet at every heavy check. A rise in bonding resistance above the limit invalidates the repair even where the laminate is sound. Report the repair to Aeralis with the thermocouple trace attached.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Surface resin loss up to 0.5 mm deep over an area not exceeding 1 500 square millimetres, with no ply damage and no delamination, may be sealed and left. Any delamination requires repair.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Bonded repair. Mechanical fasteners only at the strap ends, 12 screws AES932279K1 each end at 20 mm pitch
